title: Shadow on-call runner with telemetry playback and safe rollback hooks
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need a way for runbook authors and SREs to validate on-call runbooks against realistic past telemetry and exercise commands in a sandboxed environment without impacting production state. This PR adds a 'shadow' on-call runner that replays captured telemetry bundles into a sandboxed execution path and optionally performs dry-run vs reversible actions. The feature enables deterministic playback, automatic safety checks, and a small set of rollback hooks that undo side effects created during replay.

What this change does: adds a new internal service (shadow-runner), a telemetry-playback engine, a sandboxed action-executor with reversible action registry, a CLI for seeding telemetry bundles, and feature-flag gating so teams can opt-in. The design favors safety: destructive actions are run in 'reversible mode' and persisted changes are recorded with rollback tokens. The playback runner can be scheduled or triggered by PRs to run playbooks against a captured bundle.

High-level checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-1427. [x] core playback loop implemented and unit-tested. [x] reversible action registry with two built-in rollback handlers (user-message purge undo, synthetic-kv rollback). [x] CLI `rb-playback seed` and `rb-playback run --bundle` added. [x] metrics and tracing added for playback latency, failures, and rollback success. [x] e2e sandbox test harness under test/fixtures that replays a small bundle. [x] feature-flag gating in runtime config and a canary rollout plan.

Backward-compatibility and rollout: The shadow-runner is entirely opt-in; default is disabled. No production request path changes for normal incident-bot consumers. The CLI and seeding tools are additive. We will enable the feature for the oncall-sim org initially (10% canary), monitor metrics (incident.shadow.playback.success_rate, incident.shadow.rollback.rate), then broaden to SRE teams.

Risks and mitigations: potential for accidental state changes if a new action is registered without a rollback handler. Mitigation: PRs that add actions must provide a rollback handler or explicitly mark the action as non-productive for shadow-runner. Tests assert that every registered action either declares reversible or is noop in shadow mode. An additional runtime safety gate will abort playback if an action invokes an I/O-write outside the sandboxing policy.

Related work: ties into ENG-1490 (playbook QA harness) and SUP-1887 (customer-replay-request workflow).

merge_details: Merged by Morgan Lee via squash merge. Squashed into single commit 9h3k5b and pushed to main. Canary enabled for org:oncall-sim via feature flag. Rollout note: monitor incident.shadow.playback.success_rate for two days before expanding.
release_notes: Adds experimental shadow-runner: a sandboxed on-call runner that can replay captured telemetry bundles against runbooks for QA and validation. Includes reversible action registry and CLI tools to seed/run bundles. Disabled by default; opt-in behind feature-flag. See incident-bot/docs/shadow-runner.md for usage and safety guidelines.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature-flag. Seed small test bundle (tools/rb-playback seed --sample) before flipping canary. Observe metrics and if rollback.rate > 0.05 or errors spike, flip feature off immediately and open SUP ticket.
qa_steps: 1) Run `rb-playback seed --file test/fixtures/sample_bundle.json` 2) `rb-playback run --bundle <id> --mode shadow` 3) Confirm no production side effects and check metrics incident.shadow.playback.* 4) Test abort via POST /shadow-runner/abort with admin token
discussion_summary: Team discussion focused on safety-first design. We agreed to require explicit rollback handlers for any action added going forward, gate by feature-flag, and limit initial rollout to a small canary. Documentation and a quick ops runbook were added to reduce accidental misuse.
